judged_text: The handler persists the new attendees (lines 92-105) before updateCalendarAttendees with no compensation, so a calendar-API failure leaves the database mutated while the mutation returns an error. When the calendar provider rejects the update, the guests are already stored; the organizer retries and now gets BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests are existing attendees, leaving a half-applied state with a misleading error and no calendar update.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` (lines ~92-105), and only afterwards it calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` (near the end). There is no transaction/rollback or compensation if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, so a calendar-provider failure will leave the booking’s attendees persisted while the mutation errors. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed against the original `booking.attendees` loaded before the update, but the next run will load the now-updated attendees and `uniqueGuests.length === 0` will trigger `TRPCError(BAD_REQUEST, "emails_must_be_unique_valid")`, matching the described half-applied state and misleading error.
